title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page continues a 'digression on group formalism' (§9 of the notes on the 'équation des lacets'). The motivating situation (1) is a group G with a normal subgroup 𝔊 and a subgroup N with N → G/𝔊 surjective, so N/SN ≅ G/𝔊, where SN = N ∩ 𝔊. Grothendieck wants to rebuild G from intrinsic data (2): groups 𝔊 and N, a normal subgroup SN ⊲ N, an action θ: N → Aut(𝔊), and a homomorphism φ: SN → 𝔊. These satisfy (3a): the action of SN through θ is conjugation by φ(u). They also satisfy (3b): φ is N-equivariant, where N acts on SN by conjugation.

Steps on this page:
- (4) Form S₀G = 𝔊 ⋊ N, the semidirect product, written N.𝔊.
- (5) Define i: SN → S₀G by u ↦ u·φ(u)^{-1}.
- (*) By (3a), u x u^{-1} = φ(u) x φ(u)^{-1} in S₀G for x ∈ 𝔊. In particular u commutes with φ(u), so u·φ(u)^{-1} = φ(u)^{-1}·u.
- He checks that i is a homomorphism. Write i(u')i(u) = u'u (u^{-1}φ(u')^{-1}u) φ(u)^{-1}. By (*), u^{-1}φ(u'^{-1})u = φ(u^{-1})φ(u'^{-1})φ(u), which gives u'u φ((u'u)^{-1}) = i(u'u).
- (6) Using (3b) and SN ⊲ N, for a ∈ N: a·i(u)·a^{-1} = (aua^{-1})·φ(au^{-1}a^{-1}) = i(aua^{-1}). So i is N-equivariant and its image is normalized by N.
- The image also commutes elementwise with 𝔊: u and φ(u) act identically on 𝔊 by (3a), so u φ(u)^{-1} centralizes 𝔊.
- Hence i(SN) is normal in S₀G = 𝔊·N.

The next page then defines G := (𝔊 ⋊ N)/i(SN). This is the pushout of N ← SN → 𝔊 in groups compatible with the action, i.e. the amalgamated semidirect product. It yields:
- a commutative square SN → N, SN → 𝔊, both mapping to G;
- 𝔊 maps onto a normal subgroup of G, with N/SN ≅ G/𝔊;
- ker(φ_SN) ≅ ker(φ_N), so N ↪ G iff SN ↪ 𝔊;
- an equivalence of categories (possibly 2-categories) between the two kinds of data.

Purpose: this is a bookkeeping device for describing groups like Galois / Teichmüller-type groups (G an arithmetic group, 𝔊 a geometric fundamental group, N a subgroup such as a stabilizer or normalizer) from the 'lacets' data.
errors: Minor slip: 'N soit distingué dans N' should read 'SN distingué dans N'.
The reference 'l'image de (4)' should be the image of the homomorphism (5).
S₀G is called a 'produit direct' in the transcription. It must be the semidirect product 𝔊 ⋊ N via θ; the handwriting likely says semi-direct.
Otherwise the computations (homomorphism property, N-equivariance, centralizing 𝔊) are correct.

ideas.what: Reconstruction of G from (𝔊, N, SN ⊲ N, θ: N→Aut 𝔊, φ: SN→𝔊) with compatibility conditions, as (𝔊 ⋊ N)/{u φ(u)^{-1}}
ideas.modern_name: amalgamated semidirect product / pushout of groups along a crossed-module-type datum; standard construction of extensions from a subgroup surjecting onto the quotient
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical group theory (Schreier extension theory; Whitehead/Brown crossed modules framework)
ideas.where_published: Similar formalisms appear around SGA 1 exp. XIII / La Longue Marche context, but not this exact digression to my knowledge

ideas.what: Verification that u ↦ u φ(u)^{-1} is a homomorphism whose image is normal (N-equivariant and centralizing 𝔊)
ideas.modern_name: graph-type normal subgroup in a semidirect product

deep.surprise_reason: A careful but entirely standard group-theoretic construction (semidirect product modulo the anti-graph of φ). It is correct and well known. Its only interest is as part of the bookkeeping for the 'équation des lacets' notes.
transcription_corrections: '(produit direct [?])' is most likely '(produit semi-direct)'; mathematically it must be the semidirect product 𝔊 ⋊ N.
'le fait que N soit distingué dans N' should read 'SN soit distingué dans N'.
'l'image de (4)' refers to the image of the map (5) (i(SN)).
In (6) the second underbrace reads 'a φ(u^{-1}) a^{-1} = φ(a u^{-1} a^{-1})' (the transcription duplicates it).
